stem: Why is bedside glucose testing often included when a child presents acutely unwell?

options.text: Diabetes in children usually presents with a distinctive rash
Diabetes can present non-specifically in acutely unwell children
Only children with a family history of diabetes require glucose testing when unwell
Glucose testing is needed only if nocturnal enuresis is present
Bedside glucose testing is reserved for children with known diabetes

explanation: Diabetes can present non-specifically in acutely unwell children, so bedside glucose testing is often included to avoid missing an important diagnosis.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Diabetes in Children and Adolescents Clinical Practice Guidelines: Diabetes Mellitus: new presentation

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because diabetes does not usually present with a distinctive rash in children.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because diabetes can present non-specifically in acutely unwell children, so a bedside glucose check helps detect it early.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because glucose testing should not be limited to children with a family history of diabetes.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because nocturnal enuresis is not required before checking a child’s blood glucose.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because glucose testing is also important in acutely unwell children without known diabetes.
